name: fd-harvestcore-recordintegrity

decision_lens: A finding earns report only if it changes which record survives, which record gets picked as a cluster head, or whether a record can be lost or double-counted across two machines' harvests — trace every claim through one concrete two-machine timeline (Mac harvests, zklw harvests later, Mac pulls), not through the prose in isolation.

This agent's assigned slice is item (1)'s Python half (Task 10, Task 11) plus item (5) in full (Task 9's accretive index, Task 12's audit), applying item (6) only within that slice.
review_areas: Task 10's attribution join key: `harvest/stats.py` matches ledger attribution rows to index records by `lens == name`, not by `id`/`body_hash` — since Task 9's merge groups by `body_hash` and multiple distinct hashes can carry the identical `name` (e.g. two edits of the same `fd-x.md`, scanned before and after a rewrite), determine whether every record sharing a name receives byte-identical `findings`/`upheld`/`refuted`/`hit_rate`/`smoothed_hit_rate`, and whether that identity makes Task 12's 'head = highest `stats.smoothed_hit_rate` among members having `adjudicated>=2`' rule a real discriminator among a cluster's members or a no-op that silently falls through to the id tie-break while still being reported as `head_selected_by: "hit_rate"`.

Task 9's accretive-index invariants under two-machine merge: confirm `accessioned_at` truly never changes once set, `sightings_seen` is truly monotonic, and that a `body_hash` appearing in an older `harvest/clavain.jsonl` and a newer `harvest/zklw.jsonl` merges into exactly one `index.jsonl` row with `machines:["clavain","zklw"]` rather than two — also trace what a partially-written or mid-write-interrupted per-machine harvest file does to `merge.py`'s read (silently dropped trailing line vs. loud parse failure).

Task 11's incremental re-embed skip logic: the `<layer>.hashes.json` id-map that decides which rows are unchanged and can be skipped is keyed on `body_hash` per the spec text — but `thresholds.embedding_text` branches on whether a spec is attached (Task 8), so a record whose `body_hash` is unchanged but which newly gains a `spec_path` on a later harvest would have its actual embedding INPUT text change without its hash changing; determine whether the skip logic re-embeds this record or silently keeps a stale vector.

Task 12's `variant-of` clustering and 'regenerated wholesale on every run' head reassignment: confirm the wholesale regeneration can never orphan an `embodies`/`fused-from` edge that targets a demoted former head's record id (the spec states these edges target 'content-addressed record ids, never heads'), including for `fused-from` edges that are explicitly 'resolved by name through the cluster head' at construction time — a name-through-head resolution baked in at construction could still encode a head choice a later reassignment invalidates.

`python3 -m harvest audit`'s actual coverage (Task 12): its checklist (body/embedding-row presence, `on_disk:false` expectedness, edge-endpoint existence, exactly-one-head-per-cluster, `hash_recipe` match) — determine whether this list actually catches the two failure modes the goal singles out (a record lost across the two machines' harvest files, and a record duplicated across them), or only catches orphan-file symptoms after the fact, and whether 'every cluster has exactly one head' can still pass audit even when head selection degenerated to an id tie-break per the first review area.

Cross-check Task 10's Laplace smoothing (`(upheld+1)/(adjudicated+2)`) and its null-guard (`adjudicated>=1`) against what Task 12's calibration report (the ten closest non-merged and ten farthest merged pairs) actually reads — confirm the report generation only ever runs after Task 10 has populated `stats`, not against the zero-shape Task 9 writes on a fresh registry, and that a `--plan`/dry-run invocation can't read stats fields that don't exist yet.

severity_examples.scenario: The name-keyed attribution scheme (Task 10) means Task 12's hit-rate-based cluster-head selection can silently degenerate to arbitrary id-ordering for every cluster whose members share a name — the common case, since clustering exists precisely to group near-duplicate rewrites of the same fd-* lens. Concrete scenario: `fd-authplatform-migration` is rewritten three times across two machines (three distinct `body_hash` records, one name); a melange run adjudicates 40 findings generically against "fd-authplatform-migration"; all three records inherit `hit_rate=0.9, adjudicated=40` identically; Task 12 reports `head_selected_by: "hit_rate"` for whichever record happens to sort last by id, even though the evidence says nothing about which BODY produced the good results — the entire empirical purpose of variant clustering (reward the better-performing rewrite) silently fails.
severity_examples.condition: A cluster has ≥2 members sharing one `name`, and at least one ledger run adjudicated findings against that name (the common, intended case for clustering to matter).

severity_examples.scenario: If `merge.py`'s per-machine-file read races a concurrent write — e.g. the Mac's on-demand `harvest scan` runs while `harvest-and-push.sh` is mid-merge from a timer, or a scan is interrupted leaving a truncated final JSONL line — the read path's handling of that partial line determines whether the run fails loudly (safe) or a line-filtering reader (`filter(Boolean)`-style) silently drops the last-scanned sighting for that record, which is exactly the loss the accretive design's core promise (nothing removed except by explicit prune) exists to prevent.
severity_examples.condition: A `data/harvest/<machine>.jsonl` write is interrupted or races a concurrent reader, and `merge.py`'s JSONL parsing does not distinguish a truncated line from a legitimately absent one.

severity_examples.scenario: `harvest/embed.py`'s incremental skip-list, keyed by `body_hash` via `<layer>.hashes.json`, does not account for `embedding_text` changing independent of `body_hash` (a spec file attaching to a previously spec-less record on a later harvest) — a record could keep a stale embedding vector indefinitely once its hash is marked 'seen,' feeding Task 12's cosine-based clustering and Task 13's `resolveLens` with a vector that no longer represents the record's actual embedding input.
severity_examples.condition: A record is first harvested with no matching spec (body-fallback embedding text), then a matching spec file appears in a later harvest without the body itself changing.
